sentences.text: Ms Som Pan Products Pvt. Ltd. vs State Of Uttarakhand on 3

Author: Sudhanshu Dhulia
Bench: Sudhanshu Dhulia
In The High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 Criminal Misc. Application No.1469 of 2017
 (under Section 482 Cr.P.C.)
M/s Som Pan Products Private Limited ..........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand .........Respondent
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate, present for the applicant.
2.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Ms. Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder, present for the State/respondent.

3. A complaint has been filed by the respondent against the present applicant under Section 26 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, on which the learned Magistrate took cognizance in the matter and issued summon against the applicant.
Aggrieved, the applicant preferred a revision before the revisional court, which was dismissed by the revisional court vide order dated 07.01.2016.
Hence, the present application under Section 482 CrPC before this Court.
4. The applicant has been summoned under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
The applicant challenges the summoning order on various grounds, including the lack of jurisdiction.
5. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, no interference is presently being called for by this Court.

6. However, the matter stands disposed with the direction that the applicant shall appear before the learned Magistrate, which shall be within a period of three weeks from today, the learned Magistrate shall thereafter look into all the legal and factual submissions raised by the applicant and thereafter proceed in the matter in accordance with law.
7.

It is, however, made clear that merely because the revision against the summoning order has been dismissed by the revisional court, it will not prejudice the learned Magistrate in proceeding in the matter in accordance with law.

(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.) 03.11.2017 Ankit/
